answer: Hardware custody challenge. Each agent identity must answer a timing challenge from a physically unclonable circuit bound to one device, where responses embed a per-device delta measured at manufacture. A valid reply also requires presenting nectar tokens harvested through sustained device-local thermal work. Any second identity on the same silicon collides with the first, since the sparrow routine cross-checks oscillator drift against the enrolled profile. Cloning costs a full fabrication run per identity, so forgery scales linearly with capital rather than with software effort.
